parties.petitioner: M/s. Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd.

summary: The case involves a referral to a larger bench on the issue of whether a driving licence for a 'light motor vehicle' permits driving a 'transport vehicle' of the same weight class without separate endorsement. The referral arises from Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2017) 14 SCC 663, where certain provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, such as Sections 3 (second proviso), 4(2), 7, 14, 15 (second proviso), 180, 181, and Rules 5 and 31 of the Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, were allegedly not considered. The court observed that these provisions indicate a distinct regulatory regime for transport vehicles, warranting reconsideration. Compensation as per prior orders has been paid or will be paid. Two SLPs were excluded from referral and matters detagged.
legal_provisions_cited: Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2017) 14 SCC 663
final_judgment: Matters referred to a larger bench to be constituted by the Chief Justice of India; SLP(C) Nos.30420-30421/2019 and SLP(C) Nos.3735-3736/2021 excluded from referral; compensation compliance recorded; matters detagged.
